context_stem: For each ASL, the framework considers two broad classes of risks:
excerpt: Deployment risks: Risks that arise from active use of powerful AI models. This includes harm caused by users querying an API or other public interface, as well as misuse by internal users (compromised or malicious).
paraphrase: Deployment risks arise from active use of powerful models, including harm from API queries or misuse by internal users.

context_stem: For each ASL, the framework considers two broad classes of risks: Deployment risks
excerpt: Our deployment safety measures are designed to address these risks by governing when we can safely deploy a powerful AI model.
paraphrase: Deployment safety measures govern when a powerful model can be safely deployed.

context_stem: For each ASL, the framework considers two broad classes of risks:
excerpt: Containment risks: Risks that arise from merely possessing a powerful AI model. Examples include (1) building an AI model that, due to its general capabilities, could enable the production of weapons of mass destruction if stolen and used by a malicious actor, or (2) building a model which autonomously escapes during internal use.
paraphrase: Containment risks arise merely from possessing a powerful model, such as enabling WMD production if stolen or a model autonomously escaping during internal use.

context_stem: For each ASL, the framework considers two broad classes of risks: Containment risks
excerpt: Our containment measures are designed to address these risks by governing when we can safely train or continue training a model.
paraphrase: Containment measures govern when it is safe to train or continue training a model.

excerpt: Complying with higher ASLs is not just a procedural matter, but may sometimes require research or technical breakthroughs to give affirmative evidence of a model’s safety (which is generally not possible today), demonstrated inability to elicit catastrophic risks during red-teaming (as opposed to merely a commitment to perform red-teaming), and/or unusually stringent information security controls.
paraphrase: Meeting higher ASL requirements may require research breakthroughs, demonstrated red-teaming safety, or very strict security controls, not just procedural compliance.

excerpt: Anthropic’s commitment to follow the ASL scheme thus implies that we commit to pause the scaling2 and/or delay the deployment of new models whenever our scaling ability outstrips our ability to comply with the safety procedures for the corresponding ASL.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to pausing scaling and/or delaying deployment whenever its capability growth exceeds its ability to meet the corresponding ASL's safety procedures.

excerpt: We use "scaling" to refer to broadly increasing the capabilities and intelligence of AI systems, either through increasing compute used in training or through algorithmic improvements.
paraphrase: The footnote defines "scaling" as increasing AI capabilities via compute or algorithmic improvements.

excerpt: One challenge with the ASL scheme as compared to BSL is that ASLs above our current capabilities represent systems that have never been built before – in contrast to BSL, where the highest levels include specific dangerous pathogens that exist today.
paraphrase: Unlike BSL, higher ASL levels describe systems that do not yet exist, unlike known dangerous pathogens in BSL.

excerpt: The ASL system thus has an unavoidable component of “building the airplane while flying it”— we will have to start acting on many provisions of this policy before others can reasonably be specified.
paraphrase: The ASL system inherently requires acting on some provisions before others can be fully specified.

excerpt: Rather than try to define all future ASLs and their safety measures now (which would almost certainly not stand the test of time), we will instead take an approach of iterative commitments.
paraphrase: Anthropic will use iterative commitments rather than defining all future ASLs upfront.

excerpt: By iterative, we mean we will define ASL-2 (current system) and ASL-3 (next level of risk) now, and commit to define ASL-4 by the time we reach ASL-3, and so on.
paraphrase: Iterative means ASL-2 and ASL-3 are defined now, with ASL-4 to be defined by the time ASL-3 is reached, and so forth.

excerpt: Towards the end of this document we speculate about ASL-4+, but only to give a flavor of our current thinking and early preparation (which will likely change a lot as we get closer to ASL-4).
paraphrase: Later sections speculate about ASL-4 and beyond only to illustrate current thinking, which is expected to change substantially.

excerpt: This document will be periodically updated as we learn more, according to an “Update Process” described below.
paraphrase: The document will be periodically updated per a described Update Process.

excerpt: Updates will involve both defining higher ASL levels, and making course corrections to existing levels and safety measures as we learn more.
paraphrase: Updates will define higher ASL levels and revise existing levels and measures.

excerpt: We also welcome input on this document from other groups working on AI risk assessment and safety/security measures.
paraphrase: Anthropic welcomes input from other groups working on AI risk assessment and safety measures.
